learningObjective: Read a torch.compile recompilation log, identify the guard that failed, and choose the right knob (dynamic shapes) to prevent shape-triggered recompilation.

canonicalClaims.claim: By default in current PyTorch 2.x releases (2.3-2.5), torch.compile installs shape guards on tensor dimensions; a shape not matching an existing guard triggers a fresh compilation. Passing `dynamic=True` (or activating symbolic-shape compilation) generates a single compiled graph that services multiple shapes.
conditions: PyTorch 2.3 ~ 2.5 (behavior may shift as automatic dynamic promotion evolves).
The compile cache is warm within a single process.
nonImplications: Does not imply `dynamic=True` always outperforms specialization; symbolic-shape kernels may pay a small runtime overhead.
Does not imply that all shape mismatches recompile; if automatic dynamic promotion kicks in after N recompiles, subsequent calls reuse a symbolic-shape graph.

misconceptions.claim: torch.compile default treats all tensor shapes as dynamic; recompilation only happens when dtype changes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The default behavior in 2.3-2.5 specializes on shapes; automatic dynamic activation is version- and configuration-dependent.

misconceptions.claim: Guard failures indicate a graph break; the log entry is misclassified.
misconceptions.whyWrong: TORCH_LOGS distinguishes recompiles (guard failures) from graph breaks (untraceable bytecode); they are separate signals.

misconceptions.claim: Setting `dynamic=True` is always the correct fix regardless of workload.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Dynamic-shape compilation can miss shape-specific optimizations (tile sizes, template choices); for a small number of distinct shapes, specialization can be preferable.

misconceptions.claim: Only strides trigger guards, not shapes; the log shows shape guards, so it must be a bug.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Both shapes and strides can trigger guards; shape guards are the most common source of recompilation reports.

implementationFacts: TORCH_LOGS="recompiles" prints the failing guard for each recompile event
`dynamic=True` requests symbolic-shape tracing at compile time
Automatic dynamic promotion: after N recompiles on the same axis, later PyTorch versions promote it to symbolic
performanceScenarios: Serving code that sees a bounded number of batch sizes (e.g., 1, 8, 32) may prefer specialization; workloads with a wide input distribution benefit from symbolic-shape compilation despite the per-op overhead.
